evidence: Traupman 33: cut it out, dēsine (dēsinite); dēsiste (dēsistite)

terms.gloss: cut that out!, give that up!
evidence: Plaut. Ep. 1.1.37: istīs rēbus (Lewis & Short s.v. supersedeō: “to refrain or desist from”, with the ablative)

terms.gloss: are you still at it? will you stop?
terms.grammar: pergis with -ne: “are you going on?”; often with an infinitive

phrases.latin: Pergin' autem? nōnne ego possum, furcifer, tē perdere?
phrases.english: Still at it, are you? Don’t you know I can be the ruin of you, you rascal?

phrases.latin: Pergin' servom mē exprobrāre esse, id quod vī hostīlī optigit?
phrases.english: Will you go on throwing it in my face that I am a slave, when that came about by an enemy’s violence?

phrases.latin: Ohē, jam dēsine deōs, uxor, grātulandō obtundere tuam esse inventam gnātam.
phrases.english: Whoa, wife, stop pestering the gods now with thanks that your daughter has been found.

sources: Lewis & Short: desino · Lewis & Short: desisto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 96, 102, 300, 338.
